# Strong in the Broken Places
## Scripture
"But we have this treasure in jars of clay, to show that the surpassing power belongs to God and not to us." – 2 Corinthians 4:7
## Reflection
Men love to project strength. We want people to see the polished version—the one who has it together, who never stumbles, who carries the weight without breaking a sweat. But God's design is different. He deliberately places His treasure in clay jars. Not titanium. Not steel. Clay. Fragile, cracked, ordinary.

Why? So that when the power shows up, nobody confuses the vessel with the source. Your weaknesses don't disqualify you from God's work—they're the very places where His strength becomes visible. Paul goes on in that chapter to say he's "afflicted in every way, but not crushed." That's not denial of the cracks. That's confidence in the treasure inside them.

Brothers, stop hiding your cracks. A man who pretends he's unbreakable is a man who's never truly relied on God. Real strength isn't the absence of weakness—it's the presence of God in the middle of it. Bring Him your clay today. Let Him fill it.
## Daily Challenge
Do 3 sets of 10 pushups, and between each set confess one weakness to God and ask Him to be strong where you are not.
